correctness.rationale: The normalized Haar product yields exact signed kernel-row mass. A suffix telescoping-Lipschitz identity proves coordinatewise monotonicity. The two-scalar Bellman induction works for every r_j<=1/2, and the first biased generation has fair ancestors, giving the required lower bound. A linear sensitivity calculation gives C_{d,j}. The full-matrix exact-rational checker tests these independent constructions; finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A universal sharp levelwise norm envelope and quantitative rigidity of fair splitting solve a natural robustness question for nonhomogeneous finite filtrations in every depth. The exact position-sensitive one-node coefficient is attainable and the majority-first example disproves an attractive greedy description of maximizers. These are structural results, not arbitrary finite tabulations or mere computational reproducibility.
